implementation_notes.patch_description: Isolates the Stage 3 strictness lever from the concentration cap. v4 was the cap=20 reference with OR-logic and min_opp=2 — v9 adds AND-logic + min_opp=3 at the same cap. If v9 outperforms v4, the Stage 3 lever has independent value; if not, the conviction filter strictness is the wrong axis to push.

modified_s15_standalone.description: S15 v9: cap=20 + min_opp=3 + stage3_require_both=True. OPENCLAW_S15_INSIDER_OPPORTUNISTIC=1, OPENCLAW_S12_SELL_CLUSTER=0
modified_s15_standalone.notes: Stage 3 strictness ALONE (cap=20, AND-logic, min_opp=3) REGRESSED vs v4 baseline (cap=20, OR-logic, min_opp=2). Standalone Sharpe collapsed v4 +0.28 → v9 -1.05 (-1.33 absolute). Surprising trade count: v4 had 699, v9 has 576 — only ~18% reduction despite AND-logic on Stage 3 + tighter Stage 2. Interpretation: the AND-logic conviction filter does NOT discriminate enough on the in-sample population. The classifier remains structurally inert (every seller defaults to opportunistic) so min_opp=3 is satisfied trivially on most clusters. And the AND-logic requires both stake_pass (≥10% personal stake) AND c_suite — in the real data, when 4+ insiders fire in 30 days, at least one CEO/CFO/COO/Chair is almost always present, and many high-conviction clusters have a CEO with stake > 10%. So the population reduction is mild but the survivors are NOT obviously higher-quality — Sharpe collapsed because the strict-filter survivors happen to cluster temporally even more than v4. Standalone MaxDD held tight at 3.40% (best of any version that uses cap=20). Hit rate fell 0.61 (v7) → 0.58 (v9), aligning with v6 and v4.

ablation.notes: IDENTICAL to modified_s15_standalone. Classifier still inert. NOTE: even with min_opporutunistic_count raised to 3, the classifier produces no discriminating gate — confirming the issue is upstream data depth, not a gate-threshold tuning problem.

ablation_root_cause_analysis.finding: Classifier remains inert; raising min_opportunistic_count from 2 to 3 had NO discriminating effect (the classifier returns 'opportunistic' for nearly every (ticker, insider) by default, so the count gate is satisfied by any sufficiently-large cluster regardless of threshold).
ablation_root_cause_analysis.code_correctness: Stage 2 implementation correct. Stage 3 implementation correct (verified by unit tests for require_both=True).
ablation_root_cause_analysis.v9_stage3_strictness_effect: AND-logic on Stage 3 (require_both=True) cut trade count from v4's 699 to v9's 576 (~18%). The surviving population has WORSE Sharpe than v4's superset population. This rules out 'Stage 3 strictness alone is the missing edge' — strictness does not improve the risk-adjusted outcome at the cap=20 wide-diversification setting. Combined with the v6→v7→v8 cap-axis result, this suggests the productive lever for this strategy is concentration via the cap, NOT additional conviction-filter strictness.

standalone.v9_changes_vs_v4_baseline: Stage 2 min_opp 2→3; Stage 3 OR→AND (stage3_require_both=True); cap held at 20. Result: Sharpe regressed v4 +0.28 → v9 -1.05 (-1.33). Trade count: v4 699 → v9 576 (~18% reduction). Stage 3 strictness IS NOT a productive lever — adding AND-logic to the conviction filter at the wide-cap setting REDUCES Sharpe. The conviction filter strictness axis does not have independent value once the classifier is structurally inert.

computed_suggestion_rationale: Three of six gates pass (G2, G4, G6) and three fail (G1, G3, G5). v9 standalone Sharpe (-1.05) is the third-worst of 9 versions, beaten only by v3 (-3.44) and v5 (-1.39). Stage 3 strictness ALONE at v4's wide cap (20) does not improve risk-adjusted return — it actively REGRESSES vs v4 baseline. Combined Sharpe is also negative (-0.93). The only standalone metrics improvement is MaxDD (3.40%, lowest of any S15 variant), but that comes from variance dampening via population pruning, not from selecting higher-edge clusters. The AND-logic conviction filter is not the missing lever. KILL.
